detail:
The International Essential Tremor Foundation (IETF) reports on research it funds into the causes and mechanisms of essential tremor, including a study characterizing the transcriptomic landscapes of essential tremor, conducted at McGill University and published in Nature Genetics. Using single-cell analyses of the human cerebellum, the study examined the role of different cerebellar cell types, how genetic risk factors affect gene expression in the cerebellum, and how cells derived from people with essential tremor respond to a commonly used tremor medicine.

The foundation also highlights recruitment for studies run by tremor researchers at UT Southwestern Medical Center, including a study of familial characteristics of essential tremor using identical twins and a pilot study of essential tremor. The IETF presents its grant program, which has distributed more than $1.35 million in research funding, as support for work on the etiology and pathogenesis of the condition.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about essential tremor research and clinical trials.
summary: The International Essential Tremor Foundation reports funded research into essential tremor mechanisms, including a single-cell cerebellum study published in Nature Genetics and twin and pilot studies recruiting at UT Southwestern.
takeaways: funded work maps gene expression across cerebellar cell types
twin studies probe the familial patterns of essential tremor
research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Essential Tremor: research into cerebellar cells and family patterns
